svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: How a document moves through Doc Classifier
svg.desc: Three columns. Your computer: the browser reads each original file and uploads only its text, outline and fingerprint. Your Cloudflare deployment: one durable job per document asks TypeSafe Jev and a reader model, then a rule table in code decides filed, needs review or could not process; the record is the database and the file store. The AI services: Jev returns one choice, a certainty and a yes or no per category; the reader returns a yes or no per category with a reason and word-for-word quotes. A person reviews, the browser builds folders from the originals, the person's folder moves come back as corrections, and proposals wait for a person to accept them.
svg.text: YOUR COMPUTER (CHROME OR EDGE)
YOUR CLOUDFLARE DEPLOYMENT
THE TWO AI SERVICES
Your folder of originals
PDF, Word (.docx) and PowerPoint (.pptx) files.
They never leave this computer.
The browser reads each file
The full text with page or slide markers, the
outline (headings and table headers) and a
fingerprint: a SHA-256 hash, a short code
computed from the file's bytes.
You confirm the run
Reader choice and a spending limit. For more
than 25 files, a small trial comes first.
text, outline
+ fingerprint
A person reviews
Every document with what both systems said.
The documents they disagreed on come first.
No model decides anything on this screen.
The browser builds the folders
Copies (never moves) your originals into one
folder per category, plus Needs review and
Could not process, each with a short note.
You move misplaced copies
In File Explorer, like any other file. That
move is your correction.
folder listing
(names only)
Saved category versions
Name, what it is, what it is not, examples,
plus "none of these". A run keeps the version
it started with.
One durable job per document
A Workflow: every finished step is saved;
an interrupted job resumes from the last
saved step.
1 · Ask Jev
the full text and outline, with every
category definition
2 · Ask the reader
the same text and the same definitions
(neither judge sees the other's answer)
Each raw reply is saved before it is read.
Every reply's model is checked and recorded;
a reply from the wrong model stops the run.
3 · The rule table decides
Code, not a model: the first matching rule
wins and its id is recorded. Outcomes:
filed · needs review · could not process
The record: D1 database and R2 file store
Decisions, both replies, fingerprints. The
uploaded text stays only until you close
the run.
results +
both replies
Corrections become proposals
A new threshold, an example, a "not for"
sentence or a new category. Proposed, never
applied by itself.
a person accepts or rejects each proposal
TypeSafe Jev · jev-1.13.0
A System One model: typed judgments
with calibrated probabilities, not prose.
Returns one choice among the categories
or "none of these", how sure it is, and
a yes/no probability for each category.
text + definitions
choice, certainty,
yes/no for each
The reader · a large language model
Reads the whole text. For every category
it returns yes or no, a short reason and
up to three quotes copied word for word,
which the code checks against the text.
text + definitions
yes/no for each,
reason and quotes
The AI services inform step 3. They never
choose the label, and their two kinds of
answer are never averaged or multiplied
together.
